summary.text: 右 is the common character for “right,” including the right hand and right-hand side. One disputed account proposes that the sign 又 was reused for the word “right” because the words may have sounded alike; the old object-name and sound match are not established. Other interpretations treat 又 and 口 as parts of a hand-and-mouth or ritual scene.

formation.text: The graph is analyzed in competing ways. One reading sees 又 as a right hand and 口 as a ritual prayer vessel, forming a ritual scene associated with service and assistance. Another proposes that 又 was first used as a whole sign for “right,” then 口 was added to distinguish it from 又. A phonosemantic account instead assigns 又 a sound role and 口 a meaning role. The evidence does not resolve these proposals or establish their graphic sequence.

components.text: One interpretation treats 又 as a right hand in a ritual scene; another treats it as a whole sign borrowed for “right”; a phonosemantic account assigns it a sound role. These analyses are distinct and disputed.

sound_limitation.text: The cited readings allow comparison, but do not independently establish 又 as a component of 右 or prove a phonetic role there.

sound.text: The listed Old Chinese forms are similar, but this comparison alone does not establish a phonetic role within 右.

components.text: The received Shuowen account reads 口 as a mouth acting with the hand. A competing interpretation identifies it as a ritual prayer vessel; another says it was added as a distinguishing mark. These analyses assign it different roles.

history.text: Catalogues list 右 forms across oracle-bone, bronze, manuscript, seal, and clerical script traditions, but do not date the cited oracle-bone specimen or establish a precise sequence of graphic changes.

The received Shuowen explanation describes a hand and mouth acting together and survives in versions with different component orders. Later commentary and a competing interpretation dispute this as the graph’s original construction; the textual variants do not resolve its formation.

One account proposes that 又 was first used as a whole sign for 右 and that 口 was later added to distinguish the graphs. Another gives 口 a ritual meaning. The evidence does not settle either account or verify the proposed transition.

uncertainties.text: The evidence does not establish which recorded sense came first or a chronological chain connecting direction, assistance, blessing, ritual service, rank, west, and banquet-related use.

The proposed whole-sign borrowing account says 又 was reused to write the word for “right” because the words may have sounded alike. The old name of the depicted object and the sound match are not independently established here; this proposal does not show that 又 was a phonetic component inside 右.

senses.gloss: right; right hand or right-hand side
senses.text: The character is recorded for the right hand and right side, but the evidence does not identify either as its earliest sense.
Classical citations record uses meaning help or assist. They are not dated here well enough to establish priority or development from the directional sense.
Dictionary records include uses for blessing or protection, without establishing their chronology or a semantic link to direction or assistance.
West is recorded as a sense of 右; the evidence does not date it or explain its relation to “right.”
High status or rank is recorded among historical uses, with no chronology or development established here.
A banquet-related use is recorded and glossed as 侑. The evidence does not establish whether this is an extension of meaning or a distinct word written with 右.
The modern political sense is recorded, but no date or account of its development is supplied.

limitations.text: The recorded senses do not establish the earliest Chinese use or a chronological semantic sequence among them.

If 又 was borrowed as a whole sign for a word meaning “right,” the sign was reused because the words sounded alike or similarly, rather than because “also” developed into “right.” The old object-name and sound match remain unestablished here.

overview.text: 右 means “right,” including the right hand and right-hand side. Its formation is disputed; one proposal says 又 was reused for “right” because the words may have sounded alike, though that match is unestablished.

components.text: 又 may depict a right hand, or may be an earlier whole sign reused for “right”; its role in 右 remains disputed.
口 is interpreted as a mouth, a ritual vessel, or a later distinguishing mark; these accounts disagree about its role.

relationships.text: A competing analysis treats 又 as the depiction of a right hand within a ritual scene in 右.

One analysis assigns 又 a phonetic role in 右. The supplied readings permit a sound comparison, but do not independently confirm the component identity or role; another account treats 又 as an earlier whole sign instead.
One interpretation identifies 口 as a ritual prayer vessel in 右, distinct from the account that reads it as a mouth or a differentiating mark.
A phonosemantic analysis assigns 口 a meaning contribution. The supplied account does not show that this is the same analysis as the ritual-vessel interpretation.
One account describes 口 as a later mark added to distinguish 右 from 又; the proposed graphic transition is not independently verified.
